Often read as a sign of hidden fear or of an enemy; in some traditions a snake that does not harm you is a good sign and a link with the ancestors or with Shiva.
Seen as a good sign in many families: nourishment, peace in the home and the blessing of the elders.
A friendly dog is read as loyalty and a trusted friend; a barking or biting dog as a quarrel or a worry about someone close.
Linked with Ganesha, strength, wisdom and good fortune; an elephant coming towards you is a favoured sign.
Speed, progress and energy; a white horse is read as a sign of purity and a good journey.
In popular belief, a sign of a quiet worry or a person who is not entirely open with you.
Read as power, fear of someone strong, or one's own courage coming up.
Hanuman is linked with monkeys, so a monkey is often seen as protection; it can also mean restlessness or mischief around you.
Free birds are read as good news and freedom; a bird in a cage as a feeling of being held back.
Linked with ancestors in the Hindu tradition (food is offered to crows in the shraddha rites); the reading is a thought of the family elders.
Usually a good sign: fish are linked with prosperity and, in the Matsya avatar, with protection.
Beauty, a good name and the grace of Krishna and Kartikeya, both shown with the peacock.
Clear, calm water is read as peace of mind and health; muddy or rushing water as a worry or confusion in life.
The Ganga or any river is a favoured image, a symbol of purification and of moving on; a flooded river is read as a fear of being overwhelmed.
Usually good fortune and relief, as in the farming year; heavy storms are read as an anxious time.
A large and calm sea is read as a long journey and a broad mind; a rough sea as strong feelings.
Can mean anger, passion or a sudden change; a lamp or the sacred fire is read as a sign of blessing and knowledge.
Calm, beauty and a gentle mind; the full moon is a favoured sign.
Success, energy and honour; a rising sun is a hopeful sign.
Hope and wishes; seeing a fallen star is read as a wish ending or a change.
A task or goal; climbing it is read as effort and success, and being stuck as a feeling of a heavy burden.
Happiness and good news; the lotus is linked with Lakshmi and purity.
A strong tree is read as the family and its roots; a dry tree as concern for an elder.
Peace, good company and slow progress.
Commonly read as a worry about family, money or ageing, and in some traditions as concern for a relative. Common in many countries and often linked with stress.
Long, healthy hair is a good sign; hair falling out is read as a worry about status or strength.
A worry about the family or a conflict; in some readings the loss of an old burden.
A fear of losing control or a feeling that something in life is not secure.
Freedom, ambition and joy; a favoured dream in many cultures.
Embarrassment or a fear of being judged; very common and almost always harmless.
A worry about health or a feeling of tiredness; in some beliefs a sign of recovery, not of illness.
Work and action: clean hands a good sign, dirty or tied hands a worry about the work.
Understanding and clarity; losing sight is read as confusion about a decision.
A new beginning, a project or a wish for a child; often read as good news.
Often read as a relief of feelings, and in some popular beliefs of happiness to follow.
Often read as the opposite warning: a worry that is being covered by a smile.
Often a longing for the person; in Indian belief sometimes a sign that the ancestors need a thought, a prayer or the rites of shraddha, or that they bless the family.
The wish for protection or advice; a smiling parent is read as a blessing.
A new beginning and change; not always about a marriage; a wedding in a dream can mean a union of two parts of one's life.
A new project or a new feeling; a smiling baby is a good sign.
Guidance and a good sign; many see it as a blessing on one's path.
An unresolved quarrel or inner conflict; talking calmly with an enemy is read as a sign that the matter is easing.
A memory or a wish to reconnect; sometimes a message to call.
A part of oneself you do not yet know, or a worry about something new.
Innocence and a new idea; a lost child is read as a fear of losing something dear.
A very common dream: avoidance of a problem or fear; many say the dream ends when the problem is faced.
The self, the family and security; a new or clean house is a good sign, a broken one a worry about the home.
An opportunity or a change; an open door is hopeful, a locked one a block.
How you see yourself, or a wish for honesty; a broken mirror is read as a worry about one's image.
Status and the face one shows to others; new clothes are a good sign.
Satisfaction and a sense of enough; sweets are a favoured sign.
A journey in life; missing a train is the most common worry dream about time.
Direction and control: driving well is a good sign, losing control a worry.
Progress; going up is effort and success, going down a letting go.
Knowledge, hope and the blessing of Lakshmi; a steady flame is a favoured sign.
Knowledge and a decision to learn.
A wish for contact or a worry about a message; very common in modern dreams.
A fear of being tested or judged. It is among the most commonly reported dreams, often long after school has ended.
Receiving money is read as good news; losing it as a worry about security.
Value and honour; finding gold is read as a favoured sign, and the loss of it as a fear of loss.
Self-worth and family; wearing jewellery is a sign of respect.
Small steady gains; a handful of coins is a favoured sign.
A hidden talent or hope; the search for treasure is a wish for change.
A feeling of obligation, not necessarily about money.
A fear of loss or of being deceived; it may simply be a worry about a real item.
Work, choices and trade; a busy shop is a good sign.
A good sign of peace and a wish for spiritual comfort.
A blessing and a sign of protection, often taken as a call to prayer.
Purification and a fresh start; a favoured dream.
A need for calm; and in popular belief a sign that a prayer is being heard.
Guidance; many read it as a sign to seek advice from an elder.
A sign of ending: an old chapter closing, not of death itself, in the usual reading.
A wish for a journey of faith or for change.
A call to attention and, in popular belief, good tidings.
In Indian belief, usually the end of a phase or a change, not a prediction of death; some traditions say that to dream of one's own death is a sign of long life.
A worry about control, or about a person who is travelling.
A conflict in life or inside oneself.
An unresolved worry or memory; many people say a prayer or a light on a lamp and go back to sleep.
A feeling of having lost direction.
A feeling that something stable is shaking.
A sense of being overwhelmed by feelings or work.
